why: In a gap-free run, nums[i] - i equals nums[0]. The first missing number sits right after the first index where nums[i] - i becomes larger than nums[0], and that predicate flips from false to true exactly once, so binary search finds it in O(log n).
hints: Compare nums[i] with what it would be if nothing were missing: nums[0] + i.
The predicate 'nums[i] > nums[0] + i' is false on a prefix and true afterwards. Binary search for the first true index lo.
The answer is nums[0] + lo. O(log n) time, O(1) space; a linear scan also passes but misses the point of the week.
pitfalls: Values can be negative; work with nums[0] + i, not with i alone.
Return nums[0] + lo, not nums[lo] - 1: with several numbers missing in a row (say 10 followed by 13) the latter returns 12 instead of 11.
